mainTopic: A tree planted normally and later worshipped, and how each side reads the פסוקים about destroying idols
overview: The גמרא explains that the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי הגלילי argue about a tree that was planted normally and only later worshipped: the תנא קמא permits it, and רבי יוסי הגלילי forbids it. It proves רבי יוסי הגלילי's view from the משנה's extra rule that 'anything with human handling is forbidden.' רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה also forbids such a tree, based on the פסוק 'burn their אשרים with fire.' The phrase 'under every leafy tree' only marks where idols are found, as רבי עקיבא taught. The גמרא then works out which פסוק each side uses for which law. For רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, 'burn' covers a tree planted for worship from the start, which leaves 'hew down their אשרים' free to teach the later-worshipped tree. The רבנן use 'hew down' for רבי יהושע בן לוי's order: chop the idols, conquer the land, then destroy them fully. The amud ends with the doubled verb 'אבד תאבדון' and 'destroy their name,' which the two sides read in opposite ways, and with a ברייתא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The dispute is about a tree planted first and worshipped later
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא and רבי יוסי הגלילי argue about a tree that was planted for normal use and only later worshipped. The תנא קמא permits it, and רבי יוסי הגלילי forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And here they argue about a tree that someone planted and only later worshipped. The first תנא holds that such a tree is permitted, and רבי יוסי הגלילי holds that it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its explanation of what the two sides in the משנה are really arguing about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tree planted from the start for עבודה זרה is clearly forbidden according to everyone. The argument is only about a tree that was planted innocently and worshipped later. The תנא קמא treats it like a mountain that grew by itself, which is permitted. רבי יוסי הגלילי forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: A tree that was planted first (for normal use) and worshipped only later
They disagree
The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה
Permitted / forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: Nobody here permits a tree planted from the start for idol worship. The argument is ONLY about a tree that was planted for normal use and worshipped afterward.

phrases.english: And here, regarding a tree that one planted
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the argument in our משנה between the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי הגלילי.

phrases.english: and only afterward worshipped, they disagree
The first tanna holds:
a tree that one planted and afterward worshipped is permitted,
and Rabbi Yosei HaGelili holds:
a tree that one planted and afterward worshipped is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכָא בָּאִילָן שֶׁנְּטָעוֹ וּלְבַסּוֹף עֲבָדוֹ קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes an explanation of the משנה's dispute that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: a tree planted and later worshipped is permitted. רבי יוסי הגלילי: it is forbidden.

steps.title: How do we know this is רבי יוסי הגלילי's view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we see that רבי יוסי הגלילי forbids a tree that was planted first and worshipped later.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for proof of what it just said. This short question sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 gave each side a position, but the משנה never says outright that רבי יוסי הגלילי forbids this kind of tree. The גמרא wants a source in the משנה's own words.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? What is the source?

phrases.english: From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a source for the claim in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What in the משנה shows that רבי יוסי הגלילי forbids a tree that was planted and later worshipped?

steps.title: The end of the משנה: an אשירה is forbidden because of human handling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the end of the משנה. An אשירה is forbidden because people were involved with it, and anything people were involved with is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is from what the end of the משנה teaches: Why is an אשירה forbidden? Because it has human handling, and anything that has human handling is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer by quoting the last part of the משנה, which explains why an אשירה tree is forbidden when a worshipped mountain is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A mountain grew by itself, so worshipping it does not make it forbidden. An אשירה tree is different because a person had a hand in it. The משנה then adds a general rule, 'anything with human handling is forbidden,' and the next step will focus on that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a משנה or ברייתא
A tree used for idol worship
Human handling, meaning a person had a hand in making it

phrases.english: From the fact that the last clause teaches:
For what reason is an ashera forbidden?

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ תְּפִיסַת יְדֵי אָדָם,
phrases.english: Because it has human handling in it,
phrases.notes: He means a person was involved with the tree, like planting it, unlike a mountain that grew on its own.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ תְּפִיסַת יְדֵי אָדָם אָסוּר.
phrases.english: and anything that has human handling in it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question in step 2 by quoting the משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the end of the משנה, which forbids an אשירה because of human handling and adds a general rule about anything with human handling.

steps.title: The extra general rule comes to include a tree planted first and worshipped later
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the extra phrase 'anything with human handling' adds. It answers with a rhetorical question: surely it includes a tree that was planted normally and later worshipped.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'and anything that has human handling' come to include? Doesn't it come to include a tree that someone planted and later worshipped?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its proof by pointing to the extra words in the משנה and showing what they must be adding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tree planted from the start for idol worship is already covered by the word 'אשירה,' so the general rule must be adding something more. What it adds is the tree that was planted innocently: a person planted it, so it has human handling, and it is forbidden once it is worshipped. This shows that רבי יוסי הגלילי forbids such a tree.

keyTerms.meaning: What does this come to include?
Is it not...? (a question that expects the answer yes)

steps.whatToRemember: The phrase 'anything with human handling is forbidden' is the source that רבי יוסי הגלילי forbids even a tree that was planted for normal use and worshipped only later.

phrases.english: "And anything that has human handling in it"
comes to include what?
Does it not come to include a tree
that one planted and afterward worshipped?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the proof out of the משנה's words quoted in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי הגלילי forbids a tree planted first and worshipped later (step 1).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The extra general rule in the משנה's last clause, 'anything with human handling is forbidden.'

steps.title: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה also forbids such a tree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds that another תנא, רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, also holds that a tree planted first and worshipped later is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה also holds that a tree that someone planted and later worshipped is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that a second תנא agrees with רבי יוסי הגלילי. This sets up the ברייתא it is about to bring as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the stricter view rests on two תנאים instead of one. The proof for רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה will come from his reading of the פסוקים in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: And also

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, also holds:
a tree that one planted and afterward worshipped is forbidden,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second תנא who shares רבי יוסי הגלילי's view from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה also forbids a tree planted first and worshipped later.

steps.title: The ברייתא: mountains and hills are not forbidden, so maybe trees are not either
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא reads the פסוק: the gods 'on the mountains' must be destroyed, but not the mountains themselves, and the same for hills. So one might think trees that people worship are not forbidden either.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says, since the פסוק says 'their gods on the mountains,' and not that the mountains are their gods, and 'their gods on the hills,' and not that the hills are their gods, I would understand 'under every leafy tree their gods' to mean that the leafy tree itself, when it is their god, is not included?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא as proof for step 5. The ברייתא first lays out a possible wrong conclusion: since worshipped mountains and hills are not forbidden, maybe a worshipped tree is not forbidden either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mountains and hills are attached to the ground and formed by themselves, so worshipping them does not make them forbidden. A tree also grows from the ground, so one might compare it to a mountain. The tree that is most like a mountain is one that was not planted for worship at all, so that is the tree in question here.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it says (in the פסוק)
I would understand (introduces a possible but wrong reading)
A leafy, flourishing tree

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר,
phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:
Since it is stated: "their gods upon the mountains"
phrases.notes: דברים 12:2

phrases.english: but not the mountains themselves as their gods,
"their gods upon the hills" but not the hills themselves as their gods,

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹמֵעַ אֲנִי ״תַּחַת כׇּל עֵץ רַעֲנָן אֱלֹהֵיהֶם״
phrases.english: I would understand "under every leafy tree, their gods"
to mean: but not the leafy tree itself as their god?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא that supports step 5 and opens with its possible wrong reading.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה forbids a tree planted first and worshipped later.
steps.raayaSupportSource: His reading of דברים 12:2 in a ברייתא, which compares trees to mountains and hills.

steps.title: 'Burn their אשרים with fire' shows the tree itself is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers from the next פסוק: 'and burn their אשרים with fire.' Worshipped trees must be burned, so they are forbidden, even a tree that was planted for normal use.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק teaches: 'And burn their אשרים with fire.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question with a פסוק that says the trees themselves must be destroyed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea that trees are like mountains is rejected, because the תורה commands burning the אשרים. Since the tree being discussed was the one most like a mountain, meaning one planted innocently and worshipped later, the פסוק forbids even that tree. This proves that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה agrees with רבי יוסי הגלילי.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches (introduces the פסוק that answers the question)
And you shall burn their אשרים with fire

steps.whatToRemember: Mountains and hills that are worshipped stay permitted, but a worshipped tree is forbidden, even one planted for normal use. Both רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה hold this.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up two תנאים who forbid a tree planted first and worshipped later, against the תנא קמא, who permits it. The rest of the סוגיא builds on this split.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse states:
"And you shall burn their asherim with fire."
phrases.notes: דברים 12:3

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wrong reading in step 6 and completes the proof for step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'burn their אשרים with fire' shows that a worshipped tree itself is forbidden, unlike a mountain or hill.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה forbids a tree that was planted first and worshipped later, like רבי יוסי הגלילי.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק mention 'under every leafy tree'?
steps.stepSummary: If worshipped trees are forbidden, the גמרא asks why the פסוק lists the leafy tree together with the mountains and hills, which are not forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, why do I need the words 'under every leafy tree'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's conclusion. The same פסוק that mentions the mountains and hills also says 'under every leafy tree,' and that seems to treat trees like the mountains, which are permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7 the ברייתא proved that worshipped trees are forbidden. But the פסוק puts the gods 'under every leafy tree,' as if the tree is only the location, just like a mountain. That suggests the tree itself stays permitted, so the גמרא must explain what these words are for.

keyTerms.meaning: A leafy, flourishing tree
Why do I need it? (Why does the text say this?)

phrases.english: But then, 'under every leafy tree'
phrases.notes: דברים 12:2. It is the same פסוק that mentions the mountains and the hills.

phrases.english: why do I need it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא ״תַּחַת כׇּל עֵץ רַעֲנָן״ לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 7 using the wording of the פסוק from step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that worshipped trees are forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק lists trees as a location for idols, just like mountains, so it seems to imply that the trees themselves are permitted.

steps.title: The leafy tree is רבי עקיבא's sign of idol worship
steps.stepSummary: The words 'under every leafy tree' come to teach רבי עקיבא's rule: wherever you find a high mountain, a raised hill or a leafy tree, know that there is עבודה זרה there.
steps.simpleTranslation: That phrase comes to teach what רבי עקיבא said: 'I will explain and decide before you. Every place where you find a high mountain, a raised hill, or a leafy tree, know that there is idol worship there.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the leafy tree is mentioned only as a sign of where idol worshippers like to set up their idols. It does not mean that the tree is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words are not telling us the tree's halachic status at all. They describe the places idolaters choose, as רבי עקיבא taught. So the proof from 'burn their אשרים' stands, and worshipped trees remain forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: I will explain and make a ruling
A raised, tall hill

phrases.english: That phrase comes to teach the idea of רבי עקיבא,
as רבי עקיבא said:
I will explain and decide before you,
every place where you find
a high mountain or a raised hill
or a leafy tree,
know that there is idol worship there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the phrase to a different lesson
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Trees are listed as places, like mountains, so they should be permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase only marks where idolaters worship (רבי עקיבא's sign). It does not tell us whether the tree is permitted, so worshipped trees remain forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, 'burn their אשרים' forbids even a tree planted normally and worshipped later. 'Under every leafy tree' is only רבי עקיבא's sign for where idols are found.

steps.title: How do the רבנן use 'burn their אשרים'?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן hold that a tree planted normally and worshipped later is permitted. So what do they learn from 'and burn their אשרים with fire'?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, what do they do with this פסוק, 'and burn their אשרים with fire'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other side. It asks how the רבנן, who permit such a tree, explain the פסוק that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the רבנן disagree with this proof, they still need some use for the פסוק. The גמרא wants to know which case they apply it to.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, here the group who permit a tree that was planted and only later worshipped
What do they do with it? (How do they use this source?)
Trees that are worshipped as idols

phrases.english: And the רבנן,
this פסוק, 'and burn their אשרים with fire,'
phrases.notes: דברים 12:3

phrases.english: what do they do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן הַאי ״וַאֲשֵׁרֵיהֶם תִּשְׂרְפוּן בָּאֵשׁ״ מַאי עָבְדִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view to the opposing view of the רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the רבנן use the פסוק 'burn their אשרים'

steps.title: The רבנן use it for a tree planted for idol worship
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן need the פסוק for a tree that was planted from the start in order to be worshipped.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need it for a tree that was planted from the beginning for this purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן apply 'burn their אשרים' only to a tree that was planted for idol worship in the first place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that a tree planted for idol worship is forbidden, and the רבנן say the פסוק teaches exactly that. A tree planted normally and worshipped only later is not included, so it stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different lesson)
He planted it from the start for that purpose

phrases.english: They need it
for a tree that was planted from the beginning for this purpose.
phrases.notes: 'For this purpose' means for idol worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְאִילָן שֶׁנְּטָעוֹ מִתְּחִילָּה לְכָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן apply the פסוק to a tree planted for idol worship from the start.

steps.title: Doesn't רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה need that lesson too?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה should also need the פסוק to forbid a tree planted for idol worship. If so, it cannot also teach the later-worshipped tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: But doesn't רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה also need the פסוק for this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. He also needs a source for a tree planted for idol worship from the start, so how can he use the same פסוק for the other case?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'burn their אשרים' is used up on the basic case, there is no extra source left for the tree planted normally and worshipped later. The challenge is that one פסוק cannot do both jobs.

keyTerms.meaning: For this (the same lesson)

phrases.english: And רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה too,
doesn't he need it for this?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה נָמֵי מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְהָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the רבנן's reading from step 11 against רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's use of 'burn their אשרים' for the later-worshipped tree
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He also needs the פסוק for a tree planted for idol worship, so it is not free to teach anything more.

steps.title: He agrees, so where is his source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits that he does need the פסוק for the basic case, and asks where he learns the tree planted normally and worshipped later.
steps.simpleTranslation: Indeed, he does. But then, from where does he learn that a tree planted and only later worshipped is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge. Then it sets up the next move by asking for a different source for his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'הכי נמי' admits that 'burn their אשרים' teaches the tree planted for idol worship. That leaves רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's main ruling without a source, so the גמרא asks for one.

keyTerms.meaning: Indeed, that is so
From where does he learn it?
He planted it and later worshipped it

phrases.english: Indeed, so it is.
But a tree that was planted and only later worshipped,
from where does he learn it?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי אֶלָּא אִילָן שֶׁנְּטָעוֹ וּלְבַסּוֹף עֲבָדוֹ מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the point of step 12 and asks for a new source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's source for forbidding a tree planted normally and worshipped later

steps.title: From 'hew down their אשרים'
steps.stepSummary: He learns it from 'and hew down their אשרים.' Cutting down the tree but leaving the root fits only a tree planted normally and worshipped later.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from 'and hew down their אשרים.' Which tree has a forbidden trunk but a permitted root? You must say: a tree that was planted and only later worshipped.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה a new source: the פסוק that says to chop the אשרים down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Chopping means only the part above the ground is removed, so the trunk is forbidden but the root must be permitted. That fits only a tree that was planted normally: the worship made the tree above ground forbidden, but the root, planted innocently, stays permitted. A tree planted for worship from the start would be forbidden root and all.

keyTerms.meaning: You shall hew down (chop down)
Its trunk, the part that gets chopped
Its root
You must say (this is the only option)

phrases.english: He learns it from 'and hew down their אשרים,'
phrases.notes: דברים 7:5

phrases.english: which is a tree whose trunk is forbidden
but its root is permitted?
You must say:
a tree that was planted and only later worshipped.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13 with a new פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is 'hew down their אשרים': chopping leaves a permitted root, which fits only a tree planted normally and worshipped later.
steps.confusionAlert: Both פסוקים use the same word 'אשרים,' but they are different פסוקים. 'Burn' is in דברים 12:3, and 'hew down' is in דברים 7:5.

steps.title: But the ברייתא used 'burn their אשרים'!
steps.stepSummary: The new source contradicts the ברייתא, which clearly derived רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's ruling from 'burn their אשרים with fire.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא takes its proof from 'and burn their אשרים with fire'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. The ברייתא in step 7 openly used 'burn their אשרים' as the source, not 'hew down.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 says he learns the later-worshipped tree from 'hew down.' But the ברייתא used 'burn' for exactly that case, so the answer in step 14 does not match the ברייתא's own words.

keyTerms.meaning: Takes it (uses it as the source)
The derivation, here the ברייתא's proof

phrases.english: But 'and burn their אשרים with fire'
is what the derivation uses!
phrases.notes: He means the ברייתא from steps 6 and 7, which brought this פסוק as its proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא ״וַאֲשֵׁרֵיהֶם תִּשְׂרְפוּן בָּאֵשׁ״ קָא נָסֵיב לַהּ תַּלְמוּדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 14 using the ברייתא of step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה learns the later-worshipped tree from 'hew down their אשרים'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly derived that ruling from 'burn their אשרים,' which contradicts the new source.

steps.title: He was speaking in the style of 'if it were not written'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא mentioned 'burn with fire' only because that פסוק makes 'hew down' extra. The extra 'hew down' is the real source for the tree planted normally and worshipped later.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is speaking in the style of 'if it were not written.' If 'burn with fire' were not written, I would have said that 'hew down their אשרים' is about a tree planted from the start to be worshipped. Now that 'and burn their אשרים with fire' is written, 'and hew down their אשרים' is extra. So it is used for a tree that was planted normally and later worshipped.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from step 15. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה quoted 'burn with fire' only to show why 'hew down' is free to teach something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Burn with fire' already covers the basic case, a tree planted from the start for idol worship. That leaves 'hew down' extra, so it can teach the later-worshipped tree. The ברייתא and step 14 agree after all: 'hew down' is the true source, and 'burn' is what makes it available.

keyTerms.meaning: If it were not written: a way of saying one פסוק is needed so that another פסוק becomes extra
It became extra, left free to teach something new
You shall hew down (chop down)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה is not learning the later-worshipped tree from 'burn with fire' itself. That פסוק only frees up 'hew down', and 'hew down' teaches the new law.

phrases.english: He is speaking in the style of 'if it were not written':
phrases.notes: The ברייתא quoted 'burn with fire' only to show that it makes the other פסוק extra.

phrases.english: If 'burn with fire' were not written,
I would have said that 'hew down their asherim'
is about a tree planted from the start for this purpose.
Now that it is written 'and burn their asherim with fire,'
phrases.notes: דברים 12:3

phrases.english: 'and hew down their asherim' is extra for him,
phrases.notes: דברים 7:5

phrases.english: so it teaches about a tree he planted and only later worshipped.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15 by reading the ברייתא differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the ברייתא: the פסוק it cites is what frees up the true source, not the source itself.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא learns the later-worshipped tree directly from 'burn with fire,' which would contradict step 14.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Burn with fire' covers the planted-for-worship tree, which makes 'hew down' extra to teach the later-worshipped tree.

steps.title: What do the רבנן learn from 'hew down their אשרים'?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן do not use this פסוק for the later-worshipped tree, so the גמרא asks what they use it for.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן: what do they do with this פסוק, 'and hew down their אשרים'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the רבנן and asks what they learn from 'hew down their אשרים.' This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן disagree with רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, so they do not use 'hew down' for the later-worshipped tree. Since every פסוק must teach something, the גמרא wants to know what this one teaches according to them.

keyTerms.meaning: What do they do with it? (What do they learn from this פסוק?)
The Sages, who disagree with רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה

phrases.english: And the Rabbis: this verse, 'and hew down their asherim,'
what do they do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: ורבנן האי ואשריהם תגדעון מאי עבדי ליה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the פסוק is shown to be רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's source, the גמרא asks how the other side uses it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the רבנן learn from 'and hew down their אשרים.'

steps.title: The רבנן use the פסוק for the order of conquest
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use 'hew down' for רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule: chop down the idols first, conquer the land next, and finish destroying the idols last.
steps.simpleTranslation: They use it for the teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי. רבי יהושע בן לוי said: chopping down idols comes before conquering ארץ ישראל, and conquering ארץ ישראל comes before completely destroying the idols.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן use 'hew down' to teach the order of tasks when the Jews enter ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two stages of dealing with idols. First comes quick chopping or breaking, done before the conquest. After the conquest comes full destruction. The word 'hew down' teaches that first stage.

keyTerms.meaning: The chopping down (cutting) of the idols
Conquering the Land of Israel
Complete removal or destruction
Come first, take priority

phrases.english: For the teaching of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,
as Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The chopping down of idols
comes before the conquest of Eretz Yisrael;
the conquest of Eretz Yisrael
comes before the complete destruction of idols.

steps.triggerLanguage: לכדרבי יהושע בן לוי דאמר רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן use 'hew down' to teach that cutting down the idols comes before conquering the land, while full destruction comes after the conquest.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that both sides find a use for the פסוק. The מחלוקת is about what the פסוק teaches, not whether it teaches something.

steps.title: רב יוסף's ברייתא: break the idols and leave them
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא by רב יוסף supports the two-stage order: break the altars and pillars, and leave them for now.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יוסף taught: 'And you shall break down their altars,' and leave them. 'And you shall smash their pillars,' and leave them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support רבי יהושע בן לוי. It says to break the idols and then leave them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Breaking and then leaving the idols matches the first stage: quick damage before the conquest. Full destruction waits until later.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall break down (smash)
Their pillars (stone monuments for worship)
And leave it (leave the broken idol where it is for now)

phrases.english: As Rav Yosef taught:
'And you shall break down their altars,' and leave them;
phrases.notes: דברים 12:3

phrases.english: 'and you shall smash their pillars,' and leave them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for רבי יהושע בן לוי's order of tasks.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule that idols are first only broken, and are fully destroyed after the conquest.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יוסף's ברייתא: break the altars and pillars, and leave them.

steps.title: How can we just leave them? Idols must be burned!
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges 'leave them,' since the same פסוק says idols must be burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And leave them' — can that really be what it means? They need to be burned!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the ברייתא can say to leave the idols, when the תורה requires burning them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק goes on to say 'and burn their אשרים with fire,' so idols cannot simply be left forever. The challenge targets the word 'leave' in רב יוסף's ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? (That can't be right!)
It needs burning

phrases.english: 'And leave them' — can you really think so?
They need to be burned!
phrases.notes: The same פסוק ends with 'and burn their asherim with fire.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the ברייתא brought in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The instruction 'and leave them' in רב יוסף's ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה requires idols to be burned, so it cannot be telling us to leave them alone.

steps.title: רב הונא: chase first, burn afterward
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that 'leave them' means only for now. Chase the enemy first, then come back and burn the idols.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: Chase the enemy, and afterward burn.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the challenge. 'Leave them' is temporary: first pursue the enemy, then return and burn the idols.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The burning requirement stays in place. It is only delayed until after the conquest. This fits exactly with רבי יהושע בן לוי's order: chop, conquer, then destroy completely.

keyTerms.meaning: Pursue, chase (the enemy)
Burn

steps.whatToRemember: There are two stages for idols when conquering ארץ ישראל. First break or chop them quickly ('hew down'), then conquer the land, and only afterward burn them completely. The רבנן learn this from 'hew down,' while רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה uses the same פסוק for a tree that was planted normally and later worshipped.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
Pursue, and afterward burn.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב הונא רדוף ואחר כך שרוף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Timing: 'leave them' means postpone, not cancel.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Leave them' means the idols are never burned.
steps.terutzMaskana: The idols are left only during the conquest and are burned afterward.

steps.title: Where does רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה get his idea?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view that idols are destroyed in two stages.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, where does he get this idea from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other opinion and asks what פסוק רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה uses for his view. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the רבנן learned the two-stage order (break now, burn later) from 'hew down.' רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה uses that פסוק for something else, so he needs a different source for the same idea.

keyTerms.meaning: an idea or line of reasoning
where does he get it from?

phrases.english: And רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה,
where does he get this idea from?
phrases.notes: 'This idea' is the two-stage order: smash the idols now and destroy them completely later.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling how the רבנן learn the two-stage order, the גמרא asks for רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק behind רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's two-stage approach to destroying idols.

steps.title: The doubled verb teaches two stages
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה learns the two stages from the doubled verb 'אבד תאבדון': destroy once now, and destroy again later.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from 'אבד תאבדון,' 'you shall surely destroy.' First 'destroy,' and afterwards 'you shall destroy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה reads the doubled verb as two separate acts of destroying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה repeats the verb 'destroy.' He reads the first word as the quick smashing done during the conquest. He reads the second word as the complete destruction that comes afterwards.

keyTerms.meaning: 'you shall surely destroy' (the verb said twice)
and afterwards

phrases.english: He derives it from 'you shall surely destroy':
phrases.notes: דברים 12:2

phrases.english: first 'destroy,' and afterwards 'you shall destroy.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The doubled verb 'אבד תאבדון' teaches two stages: destroy now, then destroy fully later.

steps.title: What do the רבנן do with the doubled verb?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the רבנן learn from 'אבד תאבדון,' since they do not use it for the two stages.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, what do they learn from it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the רבנן use the doubled verb. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes that every repeated word in the תורה must teach something. The רבנן already have a different source for the two stages, so this doubled verb must teach them something else.

keyTerms.meaning: and the רבנן (what do they say?)

phrases.english: And the רבנן?
phrases.notes: Short for: what do the רבנן learn from the doubled 'destroy'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the same doubled verb back to the רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the רבנן learn from the doubled verb 'אבד תאבדון.'

steps.title: Rooting out every trace of the idol
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use the doubled verb to teach that someone who uproots an idol must remove every remaining trace of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need it to teach that one who uproots an idol must root out everything that remains of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן learn a different rule from the doubled verb: getting rid of an idol must be thorough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, the second 'destroy' means you must keep going until nothing of the idol is left. It does not mean coming back later.

keyTerms.meaning: he needs it (for a different lesson)
one who uproots
to root out everything that remains of it

phrases.aramaic: הָא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְעוֹקֵר עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
phrases.english: They need this for one who uproots an idol,
that he must root out all that remains of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The doubled verb teaches that uprooting an idol must be complete, with every trace removed.

steps.title: Where does רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה learn the root-out rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה gets the rule of rooting out the idol, since he used the doubled verb for the two stages.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, where does he learn the rule of rooting out the idol?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the other side: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה surely agrees with this rule, so where does he get it? This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side has now used the doubled verb for a different lesson. So whoever did not use it for the root-out rule needs some other source for it.

phrases.english: And רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה,
where does he learn the rule of rooting out all that remains of it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the root-out rule from step 25 back to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's source for rooting out every trace of an idol.

steps.title: Destroy their name from that place
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה learns the root-out rule from 'ואבדתם את שמם מן המקום ההוא.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from 'and you shall destroy their name from that place.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה uses a different פסוק for the root-out rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wiping out the idols' 'name' from the place means leaving nothing of them there at all. So for him, this פסוק does the job that the doubled verb did for the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: and you shall destroy their name
from that place

phrases.english: He derives it from 'and you shall destroy their name'
phrases.notes: דברים 12:3

phrases.english: 'from that place.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The root-out rule comes from 'ואבדתם את שמם מן המקום ההוא.'

steps.title: What do the רבנן learn from 'destroy their name'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the רבנן do with 'ואבדתם את שמם,' since they already have a source for the root-out rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, what do they learn from this פסוק?
steps.whatsHappening: Again the גמרא asks the רבנן what this extra פסוק teaches them. This sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן already learned the root-out rule from the doubled verb. So 'destroy their name' must teach them something new.

phrases.english: And the רבנן?
phrases.notes: Short for: what do the רבנן learn from 'and you shall destroy their name'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the פסוק from step 27 back to the רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the רבנן learn from 'ואבדתם את שמם.'

steps.title: Giving the idol an insulting nickname
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use 'ואבדתם את שמם' to teach that one should give an idol a different, insulting name.
steps.simpleTranslation: That פסוק teaches us to give it a nickname.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that for the רבנן, 'destroy their name' is about changing the idol's name, not about removing the idol itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן read 'name' very literally. You 'destroy' the idol's name by calling it something insulting in place of its honored name.

keyTerms.meaning: to give it a nickname

phrases.english: That פסוק is for giving it a nickname,
phrases.notes: He means a name that mocks the idol, in place of its honored name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'ואבדתם את שמם' teaches that one should give an idol an insulting nickname.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the pattern: each side reads the two פסוקים differently, so each side ends up with a different set of rules.

steps.title: A ברייתא that reads 'destroy their name' in two ways
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that 'ואבדתם את שמם' is read in different ways. The first opinion, רבי אליעזר's, uses it for the root-out rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר says, where do we learn that one who uproots an idol must root out all that remains of it? The פסוק says, 'and you shall destroy their name.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא to back up what it just said about this פסוק. The ברייתא opens with רבי אליעזר's opinion and continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר reads this פסוק the way רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה does, as the source for rooting out the idol. This shows that the פסוק really is read in more than one way. The nickname reading comes from the other side of the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do we know?
the פסוק teaches

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי אליעזר's line proves the nickname reading. His line matches רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. The ברייתא continues past this point, and the nickname reading comes from the other opinion in it.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר says:
From where do we know that one who uproots an idol
must root out all that remains of it?
The פסוק says: 'And you shall destroy their name.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to show that 'ואבדתם את שמם' is read in different ways.
steps.raayaObject: That 'ואבדתם את שמם' has more than one reading: the root-out rule, and (in the next part of the ברייתא) the nickname.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with רבי אליעזר's opinion, which continues past this point.
